root_cause.text: The `iavf_config_rss_reg()` function in the iavf driver uses an incorrect loop termination condition (`<=` instead of `<`) when iterating over the RSS key and lookup table dwords, resulting in an off-by-one out-of-bounds read of `adapter->rss_key` and `adapter->rss_lut` and an out-of-bounds write to device registers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the loop conditions in `iavf_config_rss_reg()` being corrected from `i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4` to `i < adapter->rss_key_size / 4` and from `i <= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` to `i < adapter->rss_lut_size / 4`. The commit message explains that because `rss_{key,lut}_size / 4` represents the total number of dwords, the last valid index is `(rss_{key,lut}_size / 4) - 1`, making the `<=` operator access one element past the end.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one errors in RSS key and LUT configuration loops to prevent out-of-bounds memory access.
intent_record.what: The loop continuation conditions in iavf_config_rss_reg were changed from '<=' to '<' for both the RSS key and LUT configuration loops.
intent_record.how: This change prevents an off-by-one out-of-bounds memory read access when iterating through the rss_key and rss_lut arrays.
